meta.purpose: Frontend-ready civic recommendations derived from CityCatalyst API data and enriched with local engagement placeholders.

rankingInputs: connection to known climate action pathways
displayRules: Show high-risk adaptation pathways first when CCRA normalised risk score is 0.75 or higher.
Pair each technical risk or emissions signal with one plain-language explanation.
Offer at least one collective civic action before individual behavior-change actions.
Flag local engagement records as placeholders until validated against municipal or community sources.

citySummary.name: Porto Alegre
citySummary.plainLanguageContext: Porto Alegre is a dense city in Rio Grande do Sul with major climate priorities around flooding, landslides, heat, water security, and residential energy use.

recommendations.title: Help shape flood-resilience investments
recommendations.plainLanguageExplanation: Flooding is one of Porto Alegre's strongest climate risk signals. Residents can help make drainage, shelter, emergency response, and recovery planning more accountable to the communities most affected.
recommendations.whyItMattersLocally: The API risk assessment marks flooding as a very high risk for both infrastructure and public health in the latest 2024 assessment.

citizenActions.label: Attend a municipal resilience, drainage, or recovery planning session
Submit comments asking how flood investments will prioritize exposed neighborhoods
Join a neighborhood or watershed group working on flood preparedness

engagementOpportunities.name: Municipal civil defense and resilience planning

recommendations.title: Support landslide prevention in exposed areas
recommendations.plainLanguageExplanation: Landslide risk is high enough to justify visible civic pathways around prevention, slope monitoring, safe housing, and emergency preparedness.
recommendations.whyItMattersLocally: The current CCRA endpoint identifies landslides as a very high risk for both infrastructure and public health in Porto Alegre.

citizenActions.label: Report drainage, slope instability, or blocked stormwater channels to the city
Ask city officials to publish landslide prevention maps and investment criteria

engagementOpportunities.name: Risk mapping and civil defense channels

recommendations.title: Expand shade, trees, and cooling spaces
recommendations.plainLanguageExplanation: Heat risks affect health, infrastructure, and comfort. Tree cover, shaded corridors, public cooling spaces, and reflective surfaces are climate actions residents can help prioritize.
recommendations.whyItMattersLocally: The CCRA current scenario shows heatwave risk for infrastructure and public health. Green infrastructure is also a strong civic engagement story because residents can identify local hot spots.

citizenActions.label: Nominate heat hot spots that need shade, trees, or cooling infrastructure
Join or organize a tree planting and maintenance effort
Support municipal budget allocations for shade, parks, and cooling spaces

engagementOpportunities.name: Urban forestry, parks, or cooling-space programs

recommendations.title: Make homes more energy efficient
recommendations.plainLanguageExplanation: Homes use energy for cooking, heating water, cooling, lighting, and appliances. Efficiency upgrades can reduce emissions and improve comfort, especially during heat events.
recommendations.whyItMattersLocally: The snapshot includes residential fuel and electricity emissions examples from SEEG and EPE for Porto Alegre.

citizenActions.label: Learn which home upgrades reduce energy use and improve heat comfort
Ask for retrofit incentives that prioritize low-income and heat-exposed households

engagementOpportunities.name: Residential retrofit, building efficiency, or energy poverty programs

recommendations.title: Support safer walking, cycling, and public-space access

sourceSignals.friendlyLabel: Promote active mobility through road space reallocation

recommendations.plainLanguageExplanation: Street design is climate policy. Safer walking, cycling, and transit access can reduce car dependence while improving health and mobility.
recommendations.whyItMattersLocally: The climate action catalogue includes active mobility as a mitigation pathway with a transportation emissions reduction potential range.

citizenActions.label: Comment on street redesigns, bike lanes, transit access, and pedestrian safety
Join a mobility or safe-streets advocacy group

engagementOpportunities.name: Mobility planning consultations and safe-streets campaigns
